textual.context: Presented as a how-to explanation with a personal participation statement; whether it is a direct offer to viewers is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: The promised earning or income is tied to the account or slot-activation action, creating a reward–action relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the amount, timeframe, eligibility, fees, recipient, actual payout, or whether activation requires payment or transfer; some ASR wording and slot labels are unclear.

visual.observation: A mobile webpage describes a partner-based income structure with the visible phrases “Higher levels = more income,” “Marketing income,” partner activity, and repeated “cycles”; it also refers to access to multiple marketing programs.
visual.context: Promotional or product-interface context is visible; no explicit warning, report, parody, or denial is shown in this frame.
visual.potential_relevance: The income claim is visibly linked to participation in a partner/marketing network and progression through levels, creating a concrete reward-to-partner-activity relationship.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not establish whether viewers were required to recruit others, pay funds, or whether any promised income was actually received.

visual.observation: A displayed reward diagram allocates returns across referral lines: first-line rewards go to upline partners; the second line references 30% from four partners and 70% to the upline; the third line references 70% from each and 30% to the upline; an “xXx cycle” is described as redistributing a final reward.
visual.context: The content appears to explain a platform reward structure; whether it is presented as promotion, demonstration, or discussion is unclear from the sampled frame.
visual.potential_relevance: Specific percentage-based rewards are visibly tied to referral lines, partners, upline relationships, and repeated cycles, which is a concrete recruitment-linked reward mechanism.
visual.limitations: The frame does not show actual transfers, participant outcomes, payment requirements, or whether the diagram reflects current operation.

visual.observation: An xGold program card visibly states “4 lines, 30 partners, 1020% per cycle” and shows buttons labeled “Upgrade for 15 BUSD” and “Activate for 10 BUSD.”
visual.context: The information is shown inside a branded platform dashboard as a product/program offer; no warning or disclaimer is visible in this frame.
visual.potential_relevance: A stated per-cycle return and partner-count condition are directly connected to paying BUSD to activate or upgrade the program.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame cannot establish whether payment occurred, whether the stated return was guaranteed or realized, or what other eligibility conditions applied.

visual_context_notes.observation: The sampled sequence shows a branded mobile browser and platform interface with dashboard, partner, link, statistics, message, and NFT sections; the source framing is not otherwise stated.
Later frames show a wallet/NFT interface with Send, Receive, Buy, and Swap controls, but no completed transfer or outcome is visible.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because the narrator presents Forsage as a walkthrough that claims account or slot activation will produce income, and the displayed reward structure ties higher income to partner activity and level progression. The xGold card pairs a 1020% per-cycle figure with paid activation and upgrade buttons, connecting the return claim to participation and BUSD payment. The sampled wallet screen does not establish a completed transfer or realized earnings.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S06 is supported because the depicted earning mechanism depends on slots, team or partner activity, uplines, multiple lines, and cycle-based distributions. The evidence shows a tiered partner matrix rather than an ordinary one-level referral, and the platform also links higher levels and partner positions to more income.
